title: Where the drummer sat on the advertising truck
summary: Foster describes the drummer sitting on the right against the cab, with guitar and bass across from him.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

They always did set the drum up. Whenever they set the drum up on the back, the drum would always sit up in the, I would say, against the cab. Against the cab. The band was the truck. That's the drum. The drum would always sit.
Was that a motor truck? Motor trucks? Oh yeah. Motor trucks.

Is that right in the middle or did they put you on one side? You know the drum would always sit right in the, right in the, to the regular end. Right in the end. The trimmer would always be on the back.
Well you'd be, you'd be, you'd be behind the cab.
In the, in the middle of the, of each side sort of thing, or up against one side or the other side?
Against one side. They always set the drum on, I would say, on the, or they always set the drum on the right side.
On the right as you're looking forward sort of thing? As you're looking forward, yeah.
Looking forward to be on the right.
And then you set the drum all on the back. There's the drum all on the back. Yeah.
Well who would be, let's see, on your right you'd be facing the, where you'd go, who'd be on your left?
